the-poetical-works-of-oliver-wendell-hol: The second volume of Holmes' collected poems gathers additional pieces from 1837 to 1848 — the Autocrat of the Breakfast Table in his brilliant prime. Wit, patriotism, and gentle satire mark these verses on American life. Boston's beloved doctor-poet at his most sparkling.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acta-pilati: This 1913 reference article on the Acta Pilati — the apocryphal Gospel of Nicodemus, Pilate's supposed report. George Reid sorts its legends from history. Christ's descent into hell fills its pages. Pious fiction of the early Church. Medieval mystery plays drew on its scenes. Its hell-harrowing thrilled the faithful.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alessandro-sc: A 1913 entry on Alessandro Scarlatti — the father of Neapolitan opera. Aloysius Walter praises his hundred works. His cantatas filled the Baroque courts. Church and theater shared his genius. Music's great melodist. His Stabat Mater crowns his sacred works. Handel learned from his operas.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alesso-baldov: This 1913 reference article on Alesso Baldovinetti — the Florentine painter of careful craft. Augustus Van Cleef praises his frescoes. His Nativity graces Sant'Ambrogio. Science served his patient art. A master of the early Renaissance. His mosaic graces the Florence baptistery. Leonardo studied his landscape craft.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrea-alciat: This 1913 reference article on Andrea Alciati — the jurist of the emblems. Thomas Shahan praises his learning. His Emblemata taught in pictures. The law schools hailed his method. A humanist among the lawyers. His devices adorned the printed books. His portraits show a keen face.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anima-christi: This 1913 reference piece on the Anima Christi — Soul of Christ, sanctify me — traces its roots. Samuel Frisbee wrote it up. St. Ignatius loved its short pleas. The faithful pray it after Communion. A prayer of tender trust. Its words have fed the saints.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-lotti: A 1913 entry on Antonio Lotti — the Venetian master of sacred music. William Grattan-Flood praises his Crucifixus. His eight-part chorus thrills the choirs. St. Mark's knew his organ. Venice's prince of church music. His madrigals charm the concert hall.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aporti: A 1913 entry on Ferrante Aporti — the pioneer of the infant schools. Edward Pace honors his charity. His asylums sheltered the poorest babes. Italy blessed the gentle priest. The father of the kindergarten's kin. His method spread through Lombardy's towns. His asylums dotted the Italian towns.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-asti: A 1913 entry on Asti — the Piedmontese diocese of the wine hills. The entry gives its ancient story. Its bishops date from antiquity. The Palio still races its streets. A see of the Monferrato. Its towers crown the Tanaro valley. Its wines are famed through Italy.
